Trigger: When finalizing an imaging-plane answer such as “transverse plane or coronal plane” for a chest image, especially when the rationale mentions a frontal/AP/PA chest radiograph and no answer options are displayed.

Observable verification action: Before committing, locate a current-image observation or tool result that directly addresses the plane-defining feature: a frontal chest projection showing both lungs, heart, clavicles, and spine en face supports the coronal plane; an axial cross-sectional slice supports the transverse plane. Confirm the terminal answer uses that observed plane evidence, not just a broad modality impression or the released reference. If no current-image observation or orientation tool output is present, retrieve or rerun orientation verification and treat the answer as unconfirmed until then; a correct grade alone does not prove the procedure, as in this transcript with no observations or tool calls. If options are displayed, map the supported plane text back to the displayed choice and check that the letter and text agree; with an empty option map, skip letter mapping.

Trigger: When finalizing an image-plane answer such as “transverse plane or coronal plane,” especially for a chest radiograph whose rationale mentions an AP/PA frontal view.

Observable verification action: Check the actual image or raw imaging observation for the plane-defining feature: a frontal chest projection showing both lungs, the heart, and the spine together supports the coronal plane, whereas an axial cross-sectional slice supports the transverse plane. Select the plane only when that observed feature matches it; if no current-image observation is present, retrieve or rerun orientation verification rather than relying on the reference answer. In this case the rationale describes a frontal chest X-ray and the terminal text matches the reference “Coronal Plane,” but the transcript contains no raw image/tool observation, so the correct grade alone does not prove the procedure. Since the options map was empty, there is no letter mapping to check; if options were displayed, the supported plane text should be mapped back to its displayed choice and the letter and text should agree.

Trigger: When finalizing an image-plane answer such as “transverse plane or coronal plane,” especially when the rationale says the image is a frontal/AP/PA chest radiograph and no options are displayed.

Observable verification action: Before committing, check the current-image observation for the plane-defining feature. A frontal chest projection showing both lungs, the heart, and the spine en face supports “coronal plane”; an axial cross-sectional slice supports “transverse plane.” If the transcript contains no raw image observation or tool result addressing orientation, obtain or rerun image/orientation verification and treat the answer as evidence-unconfirmed; do not rely on the reference answer or a correct grade alone. In this case the supported text “coronal plane” matches the reference “Coronal Plane,” but the transcript shows no image/tool observation, so the correct grade does not prove the procedure. Because the options map was empty, no letter mapping applies; if options had been displayed, map the supported plane text back to the displayed choice and verify that its letter and text agree.
